I'm going to assume this is actually a question because the explanation that guy gave is terrible. Basically, say you have an SQL server which stores your users and their passwords. Your user box, when you submit, runs a select on the users table where userName=userInput and password=UserPasswordInput. Now, what happens if someone were to enter something that looks like the following?
""; SELECT * FROM USERS WHERE USERNAME="ADMIN"; --
Basically you end up with a second query running. That just selected the admin user from the users table without caring about the password. This is a problem, because your site is now expecting a user to either return or for the query to die. It gets back the admin user - It logs them in as Admin. Big problems. This is just one example, they can also use it to destroy your database, as per the XKCD comic everyone loves. The SQL in bobby's name would result in the school losing their students table, and thus all of their data.

As for XSS, an easy example of this is shittily coded chat boxes - If you know how HTML works, what's stopping me from writing <script>SomeScriptHere</script> in a chat box and getting it to run? People aware of this will delimit and escape attempts at putting in things that would be natively run by the browser, but if you're not, viewing this page could have easily made you visit another page without your consent or realizing, because of javascript. If that page happens to say, be a malware payload, you have problems. Likewise, that script could possibly be listening to your keystrokes and sending them elsewhere, or a whole range of things (Such as accessing your session data and pulling usernames and passwords off of it, as actually was mentioned in the article).
